newsitem.title: USA: Dollar surges to new highs against yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar surges to new highs against yen.

text.p: The dollar rallied to its highest level against the Japanese yen in more than three-and-a-half years Friday as concerns about a weak Japanese economy and stock market battered the country's currency.
Typically thin holiday trading volume, which has exaggerated currency fluctuations throughout the week, prompted a series of other major currency moves.
The British pound rose to a four-year high against the dollar, and the dollar climbed to its highest level against the Swiss franc in almost two-and-a-half years.

"The three trends that have been evident all year long have re-exerted themselves," said Stephen Flanagan, senior foreign exchange dealer at Credit Agricole. "We're seeing more weakening of the yen against European currencies and the dollar, a weak Swiss franc, and strong sterling."
The dollar surged as high as 116.20 yen around midday, its highest rate since March 31, 1993, before settling at 115.30. The dollar closed at 114.95 yen on Thursday.

Despite a modest rise in the Nikkei index of 225 leading Japanese shares on Friday, the continued frailty of Tokyo's stock market remained a primary focus in the foreign exchange market. The Nikkei average closed at 19,369.04 on Friday, well below the crucial 20,000 threshold.
"It's just a continuation of what we've seen," said John McCarthy, foreign exchange manager at ING Barings Capital Markets Inc, referring to the dollar's rise against the yen.
"It's a fear of the Nikkei, concerns about the Japanese financial system, low interest rates in Japan and higher interest rates everywhere else in the world," he noted.

A primary beneficiary of the yen weakness besides the dollar was the British pound. Hopes for another rate hike in Britain were fuelled earlier in the week when Bank of England Gov. Eddie George said Britain might need to raise interest rates before the next general election to keep its economy from overheating.
Higher interest rates tend to make a country's assets, and thus its currency, comparatively more attractive.

The promise of continued low rates in Japan and higher rates in Britain spurred active selling of yen for pounds, taking the pound to 196.44 yen, its highest level against the yen since December 1992.

"Even if British rates stay where they are, relative to what we think will happen in Japan, sterling is still a pretty good value," said Mark Gargano, chief foreign exchange dealer at First Union National Bank.
The pound also surged against the dollar, ending the day at a session peak of $1.6945, its highest level since October 1992, and well above Thursday's close of $1.6740.
The dollar was a better performer against the Swiss franc, which has been plagued in recent months by the sluggish state of the Swiss economy and low Swiss interest rates.
The dollar rose to a high of 1.3515 Swiss francs, its highest level since July 1994, before ending the day at 1.3485 against 1.3450 on Thursday.
Elsewhere, the dollar ended relatively flat at 1.5545 German marks vs. 1.5541 on Thursday. The dollar ended at Canadian $1.3677, up from C$1.3638.
